result: Kiss1ARH neurons co-express Kiss1, NKB, and dynorphin, which are downregulated by E2, while E2 upregulates Slc17a6 expression and glutamate release in these neurons.
evaluation: Claims C1-C6 are all supported by citations to prior published research. These claims establish the foundational knowledge about Kiss1ARH neuron molecular characteristics and E2 regulation, providing essential background for the study.

result: E2 drives a transition in Kiss1ARH neurons from predominantly peptidergic to glutamatergic neurotransmission, shifting from pulsatile to surge mode of GnRH release.
evaluation: Claims C7-C8 and C39 present the central hypothesis, while C86-C88 provide the integrated conclusion supported by experimental data and computational modeling. The transition is supported by differential E2 regulation of peptides versus glutamate (C74-C75), changes in ion channel expression (C56, C89-C90), and modeling results (C82-C85).

result: Kiss1ARH neurons are the main neurons responsible for pulsatile LH release, express TacR3 and KOR but not GPR54, and can communicate directly with each other.
evaluation: Claims C9-C14 are supported by citations to established knowledge and prior research. These claims provide essential background on Kiss1ARH neuron function and receptor expression patterns.

result: High-frequency photoactivation of Kiss1ARH neurons induces a NKB-mediated slow EPSP through TRPC5 channels, with NKB and dynorphin causing synchronized firing while kisspeptin and glutamate serve as main output signals.
evaluation: Claims C15-C16 are based on experimental data from the current study, while C17-C23 are supported by citations to prior research. Together they establish the mechanism of synchronized firing in Kiss1ARH neurons.

result: TRPC5 channels mediate the calcium-activated non-selective cation current (ICAN) underlying persistent firing, and BAPTA abolishes the slow EPSP and persistent firing in Kiss1ARH neurons.
evaluation: Claims C24-C25 and C27-C28 are supported by citations to prior research, while C26 is presented as a postulate. Claim C41 provides experimental validation from prior work. The mechanistic link between TRPC5 and persistent firing is well-established.

result: E2 increases intrinsic excitability and glutamate release in Kiss1ARH neurons by upregulating Cacna1g, Hcn1, Hcn2, and Slc17a6 mRNA expression, with burst firing generated by T-type calcium channels and h current.
evaluation: Claims C29-C38 are supported by citations to prior research and established knowledge about burst firing mechanisms in CNS neurons. These claims provide the mechanistic foundation for understanding E2 effects on Kiss1ARH neuron excitability.

result: Kiss1ARH neurons transition from silent/tonic firing in the ovariectomized state to bursting/irregular firing with E2 treatment.
evaluation: Claim C40 is based on experimental data from whole-cell current-clamp recordings illustrated in Figure 1. The data clearly show different firing patterns between OVX and OVX+E2 conditions with statistical significance (p=0.0011).

result: High voltage-activated L-, N-, and R-type calcium channels constitute the largest component of voltage-activated Ca2+ current in Kiss1ARH neurons, with peak current at -10 mV.
evaluation: Claims C42-C48 are based on experimental data from voltage-clamp recordings with selective pharmacological blockers (Figure 2). The data show clear contributions of different calcium channel subtypes with L-, N-, and R-type channels accounting for 26.1%, 25.1%, and 31.1% respectively.

result: Voltage-activated calcium channels contribute to the generation of the slow EPSP in Kiss1ARH neurons, with nifedipine, ω-conotoxin MVIIC, SNX-482, and TTA-P2 all significantly inhibiting the slow EPSP.
evaluation: Claims C49-C52 are based on experimental data from pharmacological experiments illustrated in Figure 3. The data show significant inhibition of slow EPSP by various calcium channel blockers, supporting the role of voltage-activated calcium channels in slow EPSP generation.

result: E2 decreases Kiss1 and Tac2 mRNA expression but increases Slc17a6, Cacna1g, Hcn1, Hcn2, and all voltage-activated calcium channel mRNA expression in Kiss1ARH neurons.
evaluation: Claims C53-C55 are supported by citations to prior research, while C56 is based on qPCR data from the current study (Figure 4). The data show statistically significant increases in all voltage-activated calcium channel mRNAs with E2 treatment.

result: E2 treatment significantly increases peak calcium current density in Kiss1ARH neurons without affecting voltage dependence of activation or inactivation, indicating E2 increases channel conductance rather than altering kinetics.
evaluation: Claims C57-C60 are based on experimental data from voltage-clamp recordings (Figures 5-6). The data show significant increase in current density (p<0.0001) but no change in V1/2 for activation or inactivation, supporting the conclusion that E2 increases conductance without altering kinetics.

result: E2 downregulated Kcnd2 mRNA expression encoding Kv4.2 in Kiss1ARH neurons.
evaluation: Claim C61 is based on qPCR data with statistical significance (p=0.0061). The downregulation of this opposing K+ current would enhance the inward calcium current effects.

result: SK channel blocker apamin significantly reduced whole-cell currents in OVX females, and while E2-treated females had greater overall outward current density, there was no significant difference in apamin-sensitive component or SK3 mRNA expression between groups.
evaluation: Claims C62-C65 are based on experimental data from voltage-clamp recordings and qPCR (Figure 7). The data show significant effects of apamin in both groups but no E2 effect on SK channel expression or function.

result: E2 treatment significantly increased BK channel current and Kcnma1 (BKα1) mRNA expression, as well as Kcnb1 (Kv2.1) mRNA expression in Kiss1ARH neurons.
evaluation: Claims C66-C70 are based on experimental data from voltage-clamp recordings and qPCR (Figure 8). The data show significant increase in iberiotoxin-sensitive current in E2-treated females (p<0.0001) and increased Kcnma1 mRNA (p=0.0083) and Kcnb1 mRNA (p=0.0024).

result: E2 treatment increased M current and Kcnq2 mRNA expression in Kiss1ARH neurons, with XE-991 inhibiting M current in E2-treated but not OVX females.
evaluation: Claims C71-C73 are based on experimental data from voltage-clamp recordings and qPCR (Figure 9). The data show significant increase in XE991-sensitive current and Kcnq2 mRNA (p=0.0013) with E2 treatment.

result: E2 treatment significantly reduced Tac2 expression but increased Slc17a6 mRNA, and reduced both Trpc5 and Kcnj6 expression in Kiss1ARH neurons.
evaluation: Claims C74-C76 are based on qPCR data (Figure 10) showing statistically significant changes in all measured transcripts (p<0.0001 for Tac2 and Slc17a6, p=0.0012 for Trpc5, p=0.0086 for Kcnj6).

result: CRISPR/SaCas9 mutagenesis of Trpc5 in Kiss1ARH neurons reduced Trpc5 expression, significantly attenuated the slow EPSP, hyperpolarized resting membrane potential by 7 mV, increased rheobase by ~13%, and reduced firing frequency.
evaluation: Claims C77-C81 are based on experimental data from qPCR and whole-cell recordings (Figures 11-12). The data show significant reduction in Trpc5 expression (p<0.0001) and significant effects on slow EPSP (p<0.0001), RMP (p=0.0007), rheobase (p=0.0073), and F-I curve (p=0.0007).

result: Computational modeling confirmed that decreased TRPC5 conductance increases rheobase and reduces firing, that balance between TRPC5 and GIRK conductances controls neuronal excitability, and that burst firing in OVX+E2 state is supported by elevated h- and Ca2+ currents.
evaluation: Claims C82-C85 are based on computational modeling results (Figures 12-13). The modeling recapitulates experimental findings and provides mechanistic insights into the role of different conductances in controlling firing patterns.

result: E2 treatment upregulates voltage-activated calcium channel mRNA expression and decreases TRPC5 and GIRK channel mRNA levels, and CRISPR deletion of Trpc5 eliminates the slow EPSP.
evaluation: Claims C89-C91 summarize key experimental findings from qPCR and CRISPR experiments. These are well-supported by the data presented in Figures 4, 10, 11, and 12.
